rubrics.criterion: A stored raw sample is constructed by an operation on the raw-sample type itself that accepts the captured backtrace frames, thread-name bytes, numeric thread id and timestamp (including the fixed-size thread-name buffer and its length bookkeeping), and the capture/sampling path stores samples through that operation; nothing at the capture call site assembles the record by filling its fields inline.
rubrics.rationale: The capture site in the collection layer assembling the record field by field is the constructor displacement this instance injected; restoring construction is one of the core semantic obligations of the task prompt.

rubrics.criterion: The raw-to-resolved conversion of one sample (perfmap-lookup-first symbolication with the backtrace-symbolization fallback, and the suppression of the profiler signal handler's own frame plus its adjacent frame) is provided by the module that owns the raw sample type, and the report-building loop obtains resolved samples by invoking that owner-provided conversion instead of a report-local clone of it.
rubrics.rationale: This conversion is the largest displaced behavior in this instance; it was moved wholesale into a report-layer helper that walks the raw record's fields, and the report builder calls it on every stored sample.

rubrics.criterion: The thread-identity rule (thread name when a non-empty name was recorded, the numeric thread id otherwise) exists in exactly one owner-provided place on the resolved-sample type, and each consumer of a thread identity (the human-readable text, the flamegraph collapsed-stack lines, and the thread labels of the pprof export) obtains it by calling that one operation; no export-specific copy of the rule survives.
rubrics.rationale: This instance duplicated the identity rule as a per-export-format private helper instead of the type's own operation; one of the two copies was a format-local duplicate introduced by the displacement.

rubrics.criterion: The human-readable rendering of one resolved sample (its frame sections and its thread identity line, with the same thread name or numeric-id fallback) is provided together with the sample type it renders, and the report type's debug output ends with/composes that owner-provided rendering rather than a re-implementation living in the report module.
rubrics.rationale: The debug impl of the resolved-sample type was physically relocated into the report module next to the report's own debug output, which is a whole-cloth presentation-rule displacement.

rubrics.criterion: The flamegraph collapsed-stack line construction obtains the sample's thread identity and the frames/symbols it prints through operations provided by the sampling-model types (or a single owner-side rendering helper), not by reading the sample's thread-name, thread-id and frame-list fields directly inside the flamegraph module.
rubrics.rationale: A dedicated line-formatting helper was extracted into the flamegraph module that reads the sample's fields directly; formatting is presentation behavior of the type it prints.

rubrics.criterion: Symbol records provide the display/lookup behavior the pprof export needs (demangled user-visible name, un-demangled system name, source filename and line number, each with the same missing-value fallback), and the export's string tables and function/location tables are built by requesting those values from the symbol instead of unpacking the symbol's raw name buffer or optional file/line fields and re-implementing the lossy UTF-8 conversion, demangling and Unknown fallbacks at each call point.
rubrics.rationale: The injected export bypasses the symbol's accessors with 7 direct field reads and duplicates the demangle/decode/fallback behavior in several places; the symbol is the owner of its own name/file/line semantics.

rubrics.criterion: The profiling-window timing record (frequency, wall-clock start time, elapsed duration measured from the timer's own monotonic start) is produced by an operation on the timer type, and the guard-to-report hand-off obtains it by calling that operation; no code outside the timing domain reads the timer's frequency, start-time or start-instant fields.
rubrics.rationale: The timer's own record-producing operation was removed and replaced by a guard-module helper reading the timer's three fields; the guard holds the timer but does not own its state.

rubrics.criterion: Every consumer touched by the restored owner operations is updated in the same coherent repair: the collection-layer sample storage path, the guard's report hand-off, the report builder's resolution loop, and the debug/flamegraph/pprof render paths all route through the owner operations without any duplicated transitional path remaining.
rubrics.rationale: The displacement spans two gaining modules and two losing owners; a partial repair that fixes one export while leaving another copy (or a divergence between the collection-layer hand-off and the report layer) does not restore the boundary.

rubrics.criterion: Internal plumbing that existed only to let a consumer host the relocated behavior is retired with it: the cross-module visibility widening that a report-layer conversion needed, and imports a module pulled in solely for code it no longer hosts, are returned to owner-local scope/removal rather than being left as now-meaningless surface.
rubrics.rationale: The displacement widened a model-module helper to crate visibility and added imports on the consumer side; the natural completion of the relocation is retiring that scaffolding, though a behaviorally correct repair that leaves internal visibility wider is not wrong.

rubrics.criterion: The restored operations are presented as the owning types' API: their names, doc comments and parameter choices read as first-class behavior of the data owner (so that a maintainer adding a new export format finds presentation/conversion/identity rules on the types), not as backwards-compatibility pass-throughs.
rubrics.rationale: The value of relocating owner behavior is that future consumers discover it on the owner; wrapper-shaped leftovers would restore the letter but not the maintenance improvement the prompt asks for.

rubrics.criterion: No dead or bypassed copy of any restored rule is left anywhere in the crate: no unused format-local thread-identity helper in the pprof module, no unreached inline symbol-unpacking block in the export, no orphaned timing-assembly helper in the guard's module after the owner operations take over.
rubrics.rationale: Each restored owner operation had a consumer-side counterpart in this instance; leaving the counterpart behind (even unused) keeps the duplicated knowledge the task asks to remove and hides whether the repair is complete.

rubrics.criterion: No imports or module-level dependencies that existed only for the displaced consumer-side logic linger in the consumer modules: after the repair, the reports/export modules no longer import what only their removed inline logic used (for example the UTF-8 lossy-conversion/demangling imports or model-module field access paths that no longer appear).
rubrics.rationale: The injection added consumer-module imports solely to support logic that an ownership-respecting repair removes; leftover imports are the debris trail of an incomplete migration.

rubrics.criterion: The repaired crate contains no relocation-history scaffolding: no comments or identifiers narrating where a behavior 'used to live', where it was 'moved from', or which module 'now owns' what, and no kept-for-reference duplicates.
rubrics.rationale: Instance-specific: the displacement was staged as a plausible maintenance episode; a completed repair should read like the code was always organized this way, which is what the prompt's maintenance goal asks for.

rubrics.criterion: The signal-handler frame-filtering behavior is unchanged: a backtrace frame whose symbol is the profiling signal handler (matching also the leading-underscore platform variant) and the frame immediately after it are still suppressed, exactly those frames, with the same resolution precedence that prefers a perfmap-resolved symbol over backtrace symbolization.
rubrics.rationale: The suppressed-frame rule is the subtlest behavior inside the relocated conversion; a repair that drops, duplicates or over-applies it produces plausible-looking but wrong reports, and it is characteristic of this instance.

rubrics.criterion: The four export/presentation renderings (debug text of a resolved sample, the report's debug output, flamegraph collapsed-stack lines including thread prefix, symbol order and count suffix, and the pprof sample/label/thread strings) are byte-for-byte the same as before the repair for the same recorded samples, including the empty-thread-name fallback to the numeric id in every one of them.
rubrics.rationale: The task explicitly fixes behavior while re-homing it; format drift in any output render breaks downstream consumers of those formats and is the most likely accidental regression of a rendering relocation.

rubrics.criterion: Symbol fallbacks and demangling are unchanged: missing symbol names still render as the same Unknown spellings (in the same table slots: demangled-name slot, system-name slot and filename slot), and demangling is still applied to produce the user-visible name while the raw name remains the system name.
rubrics.rationale: The export's dedup string table relies on the exact set of demangled and raw strings inserted; collapsing the two name insertions or switching which slot is demangled changes profile content.

rubrics.criterion: Timing semantics are unchanged: the elapsed duration is still measured from the timer's monotonic start instant (not from the wall-clock start), the frequency and wall-clock start time are carried over unchanged, and the report carries empty/default timing metadata exactly in the situation where no timing window exists (the guard has no timer).
rubrics.rationale: Moving the record assembly back to the timer domain risks re-deriving the duration from the wrong clock or losing the absent-timer default, which the tests only partially cover.

rubrics.criterion: Sample-construction edge behavior is unchanged: thread names longer than the recorded fixed-buffer maximum are still truncated to the buffer without panicking, thread names containing non-UTF-8 bytes still decode lossily into the resolved presentation, and the sample's identity semantics (equality by symbol addresses and thread id, the corresponding hash) are preserved.
rubrics.rationale: The raw record's fixed-size buffer and lossy decode are exactly the internals the relocation exposed; mishandling them at either end of the sample's life is an instance-specific regression.

rubrics.criterion: Feature-conditional structure stays intact: the resolution and export behaviors repaired here remain gated exactly as before (flamegraph-only code, protobuf-format-only code, the optional perfmap-resolution support, and the alternate unwinder / large depth / frame-pointer capture variants), and no repaired path gained or lost a feature gate.
rubrics.rationale: This crate's behaviors sit behind multiple feature combinations that all must compile and pass; a relocation that quietly moves code out of (or into) the wrong cfg block would only fail for some feature sets.
